chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bizanti, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said regarding the Words of Allah, the Exalted:
Then let them complete the rites prescribed for them, perform their vows…
He said: Al-Tafath is the clipping of the nails, removing dirt, and removing the Ihram from him.

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامِ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.تَفَثُ: Rites or rituals, specifically referring to physical grooming and cleaning

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'Tafath' mean in the context of Hajj rituals according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the term 'Tafath' in Surah Al-Baqarah as the physical purification of the body—specifically clipping nails and removing dirt—alongside the ritual conclusion of Ihram. This interpretation highlights the integration of bodily cleanliness with spiritual rites, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence regarding the completion of Hajj obligations.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-77 (The author of the book narrated) my father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’d ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bezanti who narrated that regarding the Words of the Honorable the Exalted God,
‘Then let them complete the rites prescribed for them, perform their vows…’
Abul Hassan (s) said the following, “The rites consist of cutting the nails, cleaning the body, and leaving the state of ritual consecration for the Hajj (‘Ihram).”
